messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — p99 streaming latency spike detected for pool 'shared-gpu-2' :fire:
incident-bot: metrics: p95=420ms (ok), p99=3.8s (breach). Error-rate unchanged. Affected route: /v1/stream -> model: rwinf-7b-quant.
incident-bot: triggered paging to #incidents and @julia (oncall).
julia (oncall): looking. seeing high iowait on hosts in pool, starting triage. :eyes:
mike (runtime): any recent deploys to shared-gpu-2?
julia (oncall): deploy-bot shows a small runtime patch 20m ago but no model changes. rolling back won't be instant.
deploy-bot: deploy 6141589000 -> runtime/kv-cache-fix applied to shared-gpu-2, user=auto-rollout.
mike (runtime): hmm, that patch touched kv-cache eviction heuristics. can you pull eviction logs?
nate (infra): pulling host metrics. host gpu-host-17 shows blkio.write_bps_device spikes and throttling, disk util ~98%. /proc/diskstats shows heavy write latency.
erika (product): any customer-facing impact? CS?
oliver (cs): some sessions reported stutter; no 5xxs yet. Customers A and B reported longer streaming stalls during long responses. I'll notify them that we're mitigating.
julia (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) identify top noisy tenant(s) 2) throttle/evacuate them from shared-gpu-2 3) temporarily route new sessions to dedicated-burst pool 4) revert kv-cache change if we confirm correlation. executing step 1.
mike (runtime): to identify: running insights query for top token-production by tenant over last 10m.``` 
query: SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as toks, avg(p99_latency) FROM stream_metrics WHERE pool='shared-gpu-2' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY toks DESC LIMIT 10``` 

mike (runtime): tenant-42 and tenant-77 are top two by tokens and they correlate with p99 spikes.
julia (oncall): awesome. nate, can infra bump cgroup blkio limits for tenant-42 to reduce throttling and avoid immediate eviction?
nate (infra): can try. current cgroup path: /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-42/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device. setting higher write_bps for /dev/nvme0n1. running:`sudo sh -c 'echo "259:0 200000000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-42/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device'`
nate (infra): applied on gpu-host-17 and gpu-host-18. observing disk util dropping from 98% -> 60% in ~20s.
mike (runtime): nice. but the kv-cache change may be causing heavier writeback churn. still want to move tenant-42 off shared pool while we investigate.
julia (oncall): initiating evacuation for tenant-42 to dedicated-burst. running redwoodctl route command.``` 
redwoodctl route set --tenant=tenant-42 --pool=dedicated-burst --reason "live mitigation: noisy-io-evac"``` 

deploy-bot: routing change applied, tenant-42 traffic draining from shared-gpu-2 over 30s. :white_check_mark:
mike (runtime): confirm: streaming sessions from tenant-42 are now on dedicated-burst; p99 for shared-gpu-2 dropped to 650ms within 90s. p95 steady ~380ms.
erika (product): summary to stakeholders ready? oliver, can you send a short customer update saying we've mitigated noisy tenant and are doing follow-up RCA?
oliver (cs): drafting message: "We've applied a mitigation to route heavy sessions off the shared pool and applied infra throttles. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline." will send in 10m.
julia (oncall): follow-ups: - keep eviction/cgroup change logs - revert kv-cache heuristics if correlation confirmed - run offline repro with tenant workload - create postmortem if SLA impact > 5min for any customer. any objections?
mike (runtime): I'll capture heap/kv-cache metrics and rollback patch on canary if we see reproduction locally.
nate (infra): started a snapshot of /var/log/syslog and dmesg from gpu-host-17/gpu-host-18 to s3: s3://redwood-ops/incident/6141592653/host-logs.tar.gz
julia (oncall): great. also toggled temporary routing policy:``` 
service-config set routing.failover=dedicated-burst --scope=shared-gpu-pools --ttl=600
``` 

julia (oncall): monitoring window open. p99 back to normal for shared pool. will keep thread open until postmortem tasks created. :thumbsup:
mike (runtime): quick note: observed eviction storm when draining tenant-42 — several small tenants experienced short-lived tail latency blips (p99 ~1.5s) as KV caches rebalanced. we should add a staggered drain in the runbook.
julia (oncall): noted. action item: add staggered-evac to runbook (owner: mike).
erika (product): product ops request: add a telemetry flag to detect kv-cache writeback rate per tenant so we can alert earlier. owner: mike + infra.
mike (runtime): will add a per-tenant writeback-rate metric and a threshold alert.
oliver (cs): customer update sent. awaiting replies.
julia (oncall): closing live mitigation — pooled latency normalized and customers notified. will open postmortem ticket and assign owners. tagging follow-ups: mike (runtime) -> kv-cache RCA, nate (infra) -> storage config review, erika (product) -> alerting/telemetry, oliver (cs) -> customer follow-ups.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation successful. incident status -> mitigated (no active SLO breach).
julia (oncall): thanks team. logging this for postmortem. end of thread. :white_check_mark:
